title: The added team
hook: A larger toy team adds work hours and coordination. How much complete work fits?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Calculate when added per-task coordination exceeds the benefit of extra available hours.

misconception: Adding available person-hours necessarily increases finished project work.
objective: Calculate when added per-task coordination exceeds the benefit of extra available hours.

claims.text: The named work is The Mythical Man-Month, by Frederick P. Brooks Jr., candidate publication year 1975.
claims.source: Frederick P. Brooks Jr., The Mythical Man-Month (1975); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: The Mythical Man-Month warns that adding people can impose training and communication costs.
claims.source: Frederick P. Brooks Jr., The Mythical Man-Month (1975); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Original stipulated intervals model: A inputs [60, 20, 0] yield 60; B inputs [90, 20, 20] yield 40. Prediction correct option 40. A finishes {A} work hours; B finishes {B}. B has more total hours, but each complete 20-hour task now also costs 20 coordination hours. Person-hours and indivisible tasks are invented; no staffing effect is estimated.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy team has 100 hours; each complete task needs 20 work plus 10 coordination hours. Finished work hours? Only floor(100/30) = 3 complete tasks fit; they contain 60 work hours.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, intervals, inputs [100, 20, 10], output 60; independent Python recomputation.

claims.text: Does it hold up? The arithmetic follows our assumptions; real-world applicability and book attribution remain unverified.
claims.source: Scope limitation, not a research verdict: only original toy derivation supplied. Publication requires independently opened book chapter and separate real-world evidence review; no effectiveness inference is made.

recall.question: A toy team has 100 hours; each complete task needs 20 work plus 10 coordination hours. Finished work hours?
recall.why: Only floor(100/30) = 3 complete tasks fit; they contain 60 work hours.
